newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner in offshore U.S. air base project.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner in offshore U.S. air base project.

text.p: Norwegian-British engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA said Monday that the U.S. Navy had been awarded it, subject to final negotiations, a contract to conduct a feasibility study for the world's first offshore air base.
A company spokesman said the initial multi-million dollar contract would take 18 months to complete, but he declined to put a value on the deal.
Industry sources said construction of the giant three-platform structure would be worth at least $5 billion.
"We have been awarded the contract by the U.S. Navy subject to final negotiations. We hope to have something concrete in the next week or so," the spokesman said.

The planned project, dubbed Sea Base, comprises three semi-submersible platforms linked together and self-propelled, and would be large enough to land fixed-winged aircraft up to McDonnell Douglas C-17s in size and have accommodations for 10,000 troops.
Kvaerner has patented the special links to be used between the platforms, which had been developed to compensate for the effects of wave motion in open sea.
Construction of the structure would largely take place in the United States with Boeing Co. as sub-contractor.
Kvaerner said it beat bids from U.S. companies Brown & Root and McDermott International.
